description.short_caption: Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid showing intracellular and extracellular gram-positive cocci.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of cerebrospinal fluid under high magnification. Numerous gram-positive cocci are visible, both intracellularly within neutrophils and extracellularly in the background. The cocci appear in clusters, consistent with a bacterial infection. The background staining and cellular debris suggest an inflammatory response.

description.short_caption: Axial brain MRI showing hyperintense lesions.
description.detailed_description: This axial T2-weighted or FLAIR MRI image of the brain demonstrates multiple hyperintense lesions in the white matter, some of which appear periventricular. The lesions are asymmetrical and may suggest an inflammatory, infectious, or demyelinating process. The image is de-identified and shows no patient-specific information.

description.short_caption: Microscopic view of cerebrospinal fluid stained to highlight cellular and microbial elements.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of cerebrospinal fluid stained with a cytological or microbiological stain. The field contains large, irregularly shaped cells with prominent nuclei stained in purple and cytoplasm in varying shades of pink and blue. These cells may represent immune or inflammatory cells, such as macrophages or neutrophils. The staining highlights cellular morphology and potential microbial elements, though no definitive organisms are clearly visible in this field.
